newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - BP sees bright long-term outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BP sees bright long-term outlook.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc on Wednesday painted a bright picture for its long-term outlook at an analysts' meeting, which prompted some industry watchers to slightly raise their profit estimates for 1998 and 1999.
Analysts said BP impressed most of all with its outlook for its upstream operations, where it forecast a strong production increase.
"It was a very powerful and upbeat meeting," said John Toalster at broker SocGen. "We will probably be upgrading both out profit and dividend forecasts," he added.
BP's chief executive John Browne said the company's target to improve annual income by $1.5 billion a year by the end of the decade could be delivered at least by 1999 -- a year ahead of schedule.
The oil group, Europe's second biggest, added that it was confident it could grow production by 5.0 percent a year over the next decade and replace higher output with annual additions to reserves.
The company, which last month reported a 30 percent increase in its 1996 profits, also said it could be producing some 2.5 million barrels of oil and gas a day within the next decade.
This would be an increase of one million barrels a day on current output.
BP expected to boost daily production in both the Gulf of Mexico and South America and maintain output from its two established provinces, the North Sea and Alaska.

"Add to that new production from the Caspian, from North and West Africa and from Asia, and we can expect a total of around 2.5 million barrels -- two-thirds higher than our current level," Browne said.
Shares in BP, however, fell eight pence to close at 702-1/2 with analysts saying the market would likely only have only been impressed by positive BP comments for the nearer future.
"It was a very good presentation, but it is a bit too early to look at 1998 and certainly at 1999, while 2000 is a long way away yet," said Rod MacLean at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"There might be some numbers moved up out to 1999, but that's not going to affect the market very much," he added.
